doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening of the Smithsonian interview and birth in Springfield
summary: Marty Nau opens the session; Woods gives his name, birth in 1931 in Springfield, and mentions an older brother.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: Funding for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program NEA Jazz Master interview was provided by the National Endowment for the Arts.
Interviewer: Marty Nau and engineered by Ken Kimery Institution Description: Transcript, 66 pp.
Marty Nau [MN]: Okay, this is Marty Nau here with the Smithsonian interviewing Phil Woods, a certain dream of mine come true. And Phil for the national record … Phil Woods [PW]: Yes, sir.
… for the Smithsonian they’d like to have you state your full name.
Gene Quill [laughs]. No, I’m, I’m Phil Woods. I was born in uh 1931. Uh, November second, which means today I’m 78 but I’m very happy to say I have the body of a 77-year-old man.
I was born in Springfield, Massachusetts. I have one brother, seven years older. And uh, any other facts you’d like to have?
